findings.impact: If any call site (currently every fixture/test call site, and any future refactor of ledger-runtime.ts) constructs LedgerService without the 4th argument, the C/D targeted expiry/READY-close reconciliation silently does not run before an assets/poles status or quantity update. Unlike B-FAILOPEN-01, this does not open a security/authorization bypass: the unchanged migration-0005 `inventory_stock_guard` trigger still blocks the write with CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION(422) if active claims exist, so omission fails closed to the pre-C/D-fix stricter behavior rather than allowing an unsafe write. It is a silent feature-availability regression, not a safety regression.
findings.evidence: packages/core/src/catalog/ledger-service.ts:18,74; only apps/web/src/lib/ledger-runtime.ts:25 wires a real reconcileStock (via reconcileLedgerProtection); every other call site (scripts/ledger-integration.ts, tests/inventory/fixture.ts, tests/inventory/real-postgres.ts, tests/stabilization/eg.ts) constructs LedgerService with only 3 arguments, i.e. omission is already the common pattern in this codebase, mirroring the exact shape that produced B-FAILOPEN-01.
findings.fix: Either make reconcileStock a required parameter with an explicit named no-op at every fixture call site (as was done for authorizeWrite), or add an explicit code comment / lint rule flagging any production LedgerService construction missing the 4th argument, so a future omission on the one real (ledger-runtime.ts) call site is a deliberate, visible choice rather than a silent regression.
findings.test: Construct `new LedgerService(pool, adminPrincipal, noopAuthorizeWrite)` with no 4th argument, create an asset with an active protected HOLD claim past its expiry, then call update() to set status='MAINTENANCE'; assert it currently fails with CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION (proving reconciliation was skipped) rather than the intended reconciled 200, distinguishing this from the unsafe fail-open shape of B-FAILOPEN-01.

scope_assessment: This is the reserved final integrated A-G review for PR9, examining the delta from the previously-reviewed head 8467d11a (base 7caf8cea) to current head f5c57ccf, with exact snapshot-hash match confirmed. Verified line-by-line: (1) B-FAILOPEN-01 correction in packages/core/src/catalog/ledger-service.ts -- authorizeWrite is now a required (non-optional) constructor parameter, invoked without optional chaining in both create() and update(), and the constructor throws LedgerError('WRITE_AUTHORITY_NOT_CONFIGURED',500) synchronously before any pool access if the argument is missing/invalid; confirmed the only production call site (apps/web/src/lib/ledger-runtime.ts) wires the real verifyLedgerWrite, and every fixture/test call site now names an explicit synthetic no-op boundary comment rather than silently omitting the argument; confirmed the accompanying unit test (tests/unit/ledger-write-configuration.test.ts) and its before/after logs (b-review-before.log failing, b-review-after.log passing) constitute a genuine before/after regression demonstration, not a restated claim. (2) C/D: traced packages/core/src/catalog/reconcile-protection.ts (new file) end-to-end -- it runs as its own transaction using the transfer role's existing narrow lifecycle rights, re-acquires the 71820600 inventory lock, re-authorizes via loadStaff + verifyLedgerWrite (same lock-order convention as the ledger transaction: 71820600 before 71820901), expires only eligible unpaid PROVISIONAL holds whose active claims reference the specific target asset/pole (directly or via a transfer piece's source/destination/receipt pole), explicitly excludes any hold with a claim pinned to an IN_TRANSIT/RECEIVED/READY transfer piece, then closes only unreferenced issue-free READY projections touching that same target; confirmed via ledger-service.ts that this reconciliation call is a separate transaction invoked before, not inside, the ledger mutation's own transaction (which independently re-locks/re-checks version) -- satisfying the "not one atomic write" requirement. Confirmed ordinary HOLD expiry (hold-service.ts command()'s unscoped expireInventoryHolds call) never invokes closeReadyTransfers, so ordinary unpaid-HOLD expiry correctly leaves physical transfer/READY facts untouched, while only the targeted ledger-edit path and the transfer service's own add()/ready() operations narrow-close READY witnesses -- matching the required fixed-allocation-vs-expiring-lease distinction. The new "receivedDay" fixed-placement query in hold-service.ts plan() correctly adds a same-day-only block for CLOSED transfer destinations (on their scheduled_date), preventing a same-day continuation loophole while allowing next-day reuse, consistent with cd.ts's explicit test of that exact scenario. (3) E: traced packages/core/src/inventory/dependency-scope.ts's transitive variant+interval-overlap BFS closure (cross-store intervals extended to 9999-12-31, non-replanned nodes outside the closure still retained as fixed witnesses via hold-service.ts's fixedIds computation) and packages/core/src/inventory/period-matching.ts's new per-day capacitated Hall/augmenting-path pre-check, confirming via its accompanying comments and the new tests/unit/period-scope.test.ts (250-case brute-force equivalence oracle plus an explicit test that per-day feasibility alone cannot substitute for the continuous-interval backtracking search) that this is a sound necessary-but-not-sufficient pruning step, not a replacement for the full witness search. All stated numeric guards (10000/1000000/240/3000/10000/100000/100000) were located in code and match the documented bounds, each returning INDETERMINATE rather than a false FEASIBLE/sold-out result. (4) G: traced QuoteService.validateVariants's single batched SELECT plus per-item family/age/tier/presence re-validation (confirmed still individually enforced via the new eg.ts test that a bad variant on a later member is still rejected after batching), and the new views()/list()/get() sharing one repeatable-read-scoped batch of owner/snapshot-hash/HOLD/attention checks per call with no cross-request or cross-user caching (each list()/get() invocation opens its own read transaction and re-authenticates via loadStaff, correctly rejecting on a stale principal.revision). Measured query-count claims (60->1 validation SELECT, 510->15 list SQL) are corroborated by the "MEASURE" log lines in both local and CI test-stabilization-eg.log evidence at this exact head.
